alt.en: An engraved page of music numbered 16, headed in script "The red red Rose" and "The Music by P. Urbani.", with staves labelled Violini, Viola, Canto and Harpsd, marked "Largo con molta Espressione", and the words "O my love's like the red, red rose, That's newly sprung in June" and "As fair art thou my bonie lass" under the voice part.
alt.es: Página de música grabada con el número 16, con el encabezado manuscrito "The red red Rose" y "The Music by P. Urbani.", con pentagramas rotulados Violini, Viola, Canto y Harpsd, marcada "Largo con molta Espressione", y la letra "O my love's like the red, red rose, That's newly sprung in June" y "As fair art thou my bonie lass" bajo la voz.

caption.en: "The red red Rose" on page 16 of Peter Urbani's Selection of Scots Songs, Book 2 (Edinburgh, entered at Stationers' Hall in 1794), the song's earliest known printing, set to Urbani's own music for voice, two violins, viola and harpsichord, with no poet named.
caption.es: "The red red Rose" en la página 16 del segundo libro de la Selection of Scots Songs de Peter Urbani (Edimburgo, registrado en Stationers' Hall en 1794), la primera impresión conocida de la canción, con música del propio Urbani para voz, dos violines, viola y clave, y sin nombre de poeta.

source: Peter Urbani, A Selection of Scots Songs, Harmonized, Improved with Simple, and Adapted Graces, Book 2 (Edinburgh: printed for the author; undated, entered at Stationers' Hall 1794, catalogued 1795), p. 16, "The red red Rose", "The Music by P. Urbani"

alt.en: An engraved page of music numbered 415, headed "A red red Rose." and "Written for this Work by Robert Burns.", number 402, marked Slow, with seven systems of voice and bass and the words from "O my Luve's like a red, red rose" to "And the rocks melt wi' the sun: O I will love thee" under the notes.
alt.es: Página de música grabada con el número 415, con el encabezado "A red red Rose." y "Written for this Work by Robert Burns.", número 402, marcada Slow, con siete sistemas de voz y bajo y la letra desde "O my Luve's like a red, red rose" hasta "And the rocks melt wi' the sun: O I will love thee" bajo las notas.

caption.en: No. 402, "A red red Rose", marked Slow, from the fifth volume of The Scots Musical Museum (1796), Burns's song set to the strathspey Major Graham, here in the volume's 1839 Edinburgh reissue, which added the line "Written for this Work by Robert Burns" under the title.
caption.es: El n.º 402, "A red red Rose", marcado Slow, del quinto volumen de The Scots Musical Museum (1796), la canción de Burns con el strathspey Major Graham, aquí en la reedición del volumen hecha en Edimburgo en 1839, que añadió bajo el título la línea "Written for this Work by Robert Burns".

source: The Scotish Musical Museum, vol. 5 (Edinburgh: William Blackwood and Sons; London: Thomas Cadell, 1839), originally published by James Johnson; p. 415, No. 402, "A red red Rose" (first of its two pages)
library: University of Western Ontario (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Engraved page first issued 1796, this printing Edinburgh 1839; James Johnson died 1811, Stephen Clarke 1797, Burns 1796, the 1839 editors (Stenhouse 1827, Sharpe 1851, Laing 1878) by 1878. The Internet Archive record states no licence or restriction. Faithful scan of a flat page adds no new copyright (see rights.md).

alt.en: A yellowed engraved page of music numbered 91, headed "Low down in the Broom.", number 90, marked Andante, with five systems of voice and figured bass, the words "My Daddy is a canker'd carle, He'll ne twin wi' his gear" and the refrain "For he's low down, he's in the broom, that's waiting on me" under the notes, and three more verses below in two columns.
alt.es: Página amarillenta de música grabada con el número 91, con el encabezado "Low down in the Broom.", número 90, marcada Andante, con cinco sistemas de voz y bajo cifrado, la letra "My Daddy is a canker'd carle, He'll ne twin wi' his gear" y el estribillo "For he's low down, he's in the broom, that's waiting on me" bajo las notas, y tres estrofas más debajo en dos columnas.

caption.en: Low down in the Broom, No. 90 in the first volume of The Scots Musical Museum (1787), marked Andante, with the older song "My Daddy is a canker'd carle": the old air behind the tune R. A. Smith printed with A Red, Red Rose in the 1820s; Graham called Smith's tune "a modern version" of the old air.
caption.es: Low down in the Broom, el n.º 90 del primer volumen de The Scots Musical Museum (1787), marcado Andante, con la canción más antigua "My Daddy is a canker'd carle": la melodía antigua de la que viene la que R. A. Smith imprimió con A Red, Red Rose en la década de 1820; Graham llamó a la de Smith "una versión moderna" de la antigua.

source: James Johnson, The Scots Musical Museum, vol. 1 (Edinburgh: Johnson & Co.; this copy's title page is the first issue, dedicated to the Catch Club and sold by N. Stewart, R. Bremner and others, pencilled "1787"), p. 91, No. 90, "Low down in the Broom"
library: University of Western Ontario (digitized by the Internet Archive)
callNumber: Internet Archive scotsmusicalmuse12john (vols. 1 and 2 bound together)
licenceEvidence: Engraved page from the Edinburgh plates of 1787 (volume 1 preface dated 1787, per the item record; this copy has the first-issue Catch Club title page, which Johnson replaced in 1803); James Johnson died 1811, Stephen Clarke 1797; the words "My Daddy is a canker'd carle" are an anonymous old song. alt.en: An engraved page of music numbered 85, headed "MY LOVE IS LIKE A RED RED ROSE.", with five systems of voice and piano, the first verse and its repeated refrain under the notes from "O, my love is like a red, red rose, That's newly sprung in June!", and the second verse printed below, ending "Tho' 'twere ten thousand mile."
alt.es: Página de música grabada con el número 85, con el encabezado "MY LOVE IS LIKE A RED RED ROSE.", con cinco sistemas de voz y piano, la primera estrofa y su estribillo repetido bajo las notas desde "O, my love is like a red, red rose, That's newly sprung in June!", y la segunda estrofa impresa debajo, que termina "Tho' 'twere ten thousand mile."

caption.en: My Love Is Like a Red Red Rose on page 85 of the third volume of R. A. Smith's Scotish Minstrel (Edinburgh: Robert Purdie, early 1820s), the earliest known printing of the song with Low down in the Broom, and the page our melody and words are taken from.
caption.es: My Love Is Like a Red Red Rose en la página 85 del tercer volumen de The Scotish Minstrel de R. A. Smith (Edimburgo: Robert Purdie, principios de la década de 1820), la primera impresión conocida de la canción con Low down in the Broom, y la página de la que tomamos la melodía y la letra.

source: R. A. Smith, The Scotish Minstrel: A Selection from the Vocal Melodies of Scotland, Ancient & Modern, Arranged for the Piano Forte, vol. 3 (Edinburgh: Robt. Purdie, 70 Princes Street; undated, catalogued 1821), p. 85, "My Love Is Like a Red Red Rose"
